title: Feature request: Add reranker support for two-stage retrieval
description:
## Feature request: Reranker support

### Problem

Currently `store.retrieve()` returns top-k chunks based solely on first-pass similarity (cosine distance) or BM25 keyword matching. In practice, the top-k results from embedding similarity or BM25 are often not the most relevant — a second-pass cross-encoder reranker can dramatically improve retrieval quality.

This is a standard technique in production RAG systems (e.g., Cohere Rerank, Jina Reranker, BGE-Reranker, cross-encoder models from sentence-transformers).

### Proposed API

A `Reranker` abstraction similar to the existing `EmbeddingProvider` pattern:

```python
from raghilda.reranker import Reranker, CohereReranker
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="docs.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOpenAI(),
    reranker=CohereReranker(model="rerank-english-v3.0"),
)

# retrieve() returns top_k after reranking
chunks = store.retrieve("query", top_k=5)
```

Or a standalone usage:
```python
reranker = CohereReranker(model="rerank-english-v3.0")
reranked = reranker.rerank(query="...", chunks=chunks, top_n=5)
```

Possible reranker backends
- Cohere Rerank (cohere SDK)
- Jina Reranker (via Jina API)
- sentence-transformers cross-encoders (local, e.g. cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2)
- LLM-based reranking (e.g., GPT ranking via pairwise comparison)

title: fix: don't invalidate cache for `CloudflareCrawler` based on a changed `account_id` value
description:
Currently we have cache invalidation for `CloudflareCrawler` based on entries in https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/3b576ca4aa1ddb1fe5dec944127a9c5f2a845d2a/src/raghilda/crawl.py#L1689

However, we shouldn't include `"account_id"` in that signature since it shouldn't be involved in cache invalidation.

title: enh: simplify `CrawlScope` pattern API
description:
Currently, `include_patterns` and `exclude_patterns` in `CrawlScope` behave very differently depending on the crawler backend. So `WebCrawler` interprets as Python regular expressions. But the new `CloudflareCrawler` forwards the values to the Cloudflare API their own style of wildcard patterns (like, `**` will match any number of path segments).

This will likely be very confusing for users. Not only this but it'll force users to write different pattern values when switching backends.

To make this better, we should unify the default pattern syntax to globs (like `*`, `**`) for both crawlers. It seems to me that globs are more intuitive anyway for URL path matching (and I think they are well understood). We can, under the hood, convert globs to regex for `WebCrawler` and keep using the Cloudflare API as it is.

An additional thing to do would be to support Python regexes for more advanced use cases. We should do this by accepting pre-compiled regexes in addition to a `str`.

A consideration for getting this work underway is choosing a glob-to-regex converter util. There's a built-in one in Python and I do believe libraries for this.

title: feat: add `render=` parameter to `WebCrawler`
description:
The `render=` parameter in `CloudflareCrawler' (`True` is the default) controls whether Cloudflare executes JavaScript before extracting page content. It is essential for site that perform client-side rendering.

Right now, the parameter/functionality doesn't exist in `WebCrawler` but it would be a good feature addition for that class.

title: `CatalogException: Scalar Function with name match_bm25 does not exist` when using `DuckDBStore.retrieve_bm25()`
description:
### Description
I am encountering a `CatalogException` when trying to use the `retrieve_bm25()` method from `DuckDBStore`. It appears that the DuckDB `fts` extension, which provides the underlying `match_bm25` macro, is not being automatically loaded or initialized by `raghilda` before executing the query.

### Reproducible Example
```python
from typing import Any, Sequence
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from raghilda.embedding import (
    EmbeddingProvider,
    EmbedInputType,
    register_embedding_provider,
)
import torch
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.scrape import find_links
import duckdb
import os



@register_embedding_provider("EmbeddingLocal")
class EmbeddingLocal(EmbeddingProvider):
    """Embedding provider using local sentence-transformers models."""

    def __init__(self, model: str = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2", device: str = 'cpu'):
        self.model_name = model
        self._model = SentenceTransformer(model, device=device)

    def embed(
        self,
        x: Sequence[str],
        input_type: EmbedInputType = EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT,
    ) -> Sequence[Sequence[float]]:
        if isinstance(x, str):
            raise TypeError("Input must be a sequence of strings")

        if len(x) == 0:
            return []

        # sentence-transformers doesn't distinguish query vs document
        embeddings = self._model.encode(list(x))
        return [emb.tolist() for emb in embeddings]

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "type": "EmbeddingLocal",
            "model": self.model_name,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, config: dict[str, Any]) -> "EmbeddingLocal":
        return cls(model=config.get("model", "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"))


model_path = r'./model_repo/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'


device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="local_store.db",
    embed=EmbeddingLocal(model=model_path, device=device)
)

# Load fts
con = duckdb.connect("local_store.db") 
con.execute("INSTALL fts;")
con.execute("LOAD fts;")

# Custom chunker with smaller chunks
chunker = MarkdownChunker(
    chunk_size=800,
    target_overlap=0.3,
    segment_by_heading_levels=[1],
)

links = find_links(
    "https://quarto.org/docs/guide/",
    depth=1,  # follow links 1 level deep from the starting page
    children_only=True,
)
print(f"Found {len(links)} pages")


for link in links:
    document = read_as_markdown(link)
    chunked = chunker.chunk(document)
    store.upsert(chunked)

print(f"Indexed {store.size()} documents")

print(document.content[:500])


print(f"Created {len(chunked.chunks)} chunks")
print(f"\nFirst chunk context: {chunked.chunks[0].context}")
print(f"First chunk text:\n{chunked.chunks[0].text[:200]}...")


# Vector similarity search only
chunks_vss = store.retrieve_vss("presentations", top_k=5)
chunks_vss

# BM25 keyword search only
chunks_bm25 = store.retrieve_bm25("presentations", top_k=5)


CatalogException: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name match_bm25 does not exist!
Did you mean "main.max_by"?

LINE 13:                 fts_main_chunks.match_bm25(chunk_id, $query, k := $k, b...
                         ^
Cell In[17], line 1
----> 1 chunks_bm25 = store.retrieve_bm25("presentations", top_k=5)
```



### Suggestion
It would be great if `raghilda` could automatically handle the `INSTALL fts;` and `LOAD fts;` commands (similar to how it likely handles the `vss` extension for vector similarity search) when a user calls `retrieve_bm25()` or `retrieve()`, preventing this `CatalogException`.

title: Feature Request: Key-Only Storage Mode (Remote Text Retrieval)
description:
Storing raw document text in the local DuckDB file is a blocker for data-sensitive environments. Teams subject to data controls may not be able to store plaintext content locally, even privately.

A "reference key mode" that persists only a reference key alongside each index entry but never writes the raw text to disk would be useful here. At query time, the caller resolves keys to content via a provided callback or some other way.

Thank you!

title: Add delete(origin) method to BaseStore
description:
## Summary

`BaseStore` currently has no way to delete a document by origin. This is a basic CRUD gap — we have create/read/update (`upsert`, `retrieve`) but no delete.

## Proposed API

```python
# In BaseStore
@abstractmethod
def delete(self, origin: str) -> bool:
    """Delete a document and its chunks by origin.
    
    Returns True if the document was found and deleted, False if not found.
    """
    ...
```

Each backend implements it:
- **DuckDBStore**: delete from documents + chunks tables by origin
- **ChromaDBStore**: delete matching IDs from the collection
- **OpenAIStore**: find and delete the file from the vector store

title: Consider supporting single-element logical filter nodes
description:
## Context

When building attribute filters programmatically, it's common to collect conditions into a list and then wrap them in `{"type": "and", "filters": [...]}`. This works well for 2+ conditions, but requires special-casing for 0 and 1 conditions since ChromaDB rejects `$and` with a single entry.

This leads to boilerplate like:

```python
if len(filters) == 0:
    attributes_filter = None
elif len(filters) == 1:
    attributes_filter = filters[0]
else:
    attributes_filter = {"type": "and", "filters": filters}
```

It would be nice if raghilda could unwrap single-element logical nodes automatically during filter compilation (before emitting to the backend), so users could always write:

```python
attributes_filter = {"type": "and", "filters": filters} if filters else None
```

## Possible approach

In `_emit_chroma_where` (and similar emitters), if a logical node has exactly one child, emit the child directly instead of wrapping it in `$and`/`$or`. The DuckDB and OpenAI emitters may already handle this gracefully, so it might only need a ChromaDB-specific change.

title: Document supported attribute filter operators
description:
## Summary

The attribute filters guide (`user_guide/03-attribute-filters.qmd`) demonstrates filter usage through examples but doesn't include a reference section listing all supported operators.

A user reading the guide can infer `=`, `>=`, `AND`, and `IS NULL` from the examples, but there's no way to discover the full set of available operators without reading the source code.

## Suggested addition

A "Filter Operators" reference section listing:

**Comparison operators** (SQL-like string / dict AST):
- `=` / `eq`, `!=` / `ne`
- `>` / `gt`, `>=` / `gte`, `<` / `lt`, `<=` / `lte`
- `IN` / `in`, `NOT IN` / `nin`
- `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`

**Logical operators:**
- `AND`, `OR`

**Dict AST structure:**
- `{"type": "<operator>", "key": "<column>", "value": <value>}`
- `{"type": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]}`

This could go between the current "Recap: Declaring Attributes" and "Built-In Backend Columns" sections, or as a new standalone section.

title: Support LIKE/contains filtering for string attributes
description:
## Summary

The attribute filter layer currently supports `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`, and `nin` operators. There's no way to do substring/pattern matching on string attributes.

## Motivation

When attributes store comma-separated values (e.g. `labels = "bug, enhancement"`), exact equality filters like `labels = 'bug'` won't match. A `LIKE` operator would allow patterns like `labels LIKE '%bug%'` to find partial matches.

This came up in the GitHub issues RAG example, where issue labels are stored as a comma-separated string and users want to filter by a single label.

## Backend support

- **DuckDB**: Native `LIKE` support
- **ChromaDB**: Has `$contains` operator (equivalent)
- **OpenAI**: Unsupported (raise an error)

title: Support retrieving with just attributes filter without a query
description:
Currently, `store.retrieve()` requires a query string for semantic search. There are cases where you want to retrieve documents based solely on attribute filters without providing a search query.

For example, retrieving all documents from the last 7 days — without needing to specify a semantic search term.

The `retrieve` method should support being called with only an `attributes_filter` and no `query` (or an empty/None query), returning matching documents without ranking by embedding similarity.

title: Add upsert support for incremental document updates
description:
## Problem

When doing incremental syncs (e.g., syncing GitHub issues that have been updated), we need to update existing documents in the store. Currently, inserting a document with an existing `origin` fails with a unique constraint violation.

## Desired Behavior

Support updating existing documents. Two API options to consider:

### Option A: `upsert` parameter on existing methods
```python
store.insert(doc, upsert=True)
store.ingest(items, prepare=fn, upsert=True)
```
- When `upsert=False` (default): Current behavior - fail on duplicate origin
- When `upsert=True`: Delete existing document with same origin before inserting

### Option B: Separate `update` method
```python
store.update(doc)  # Fails if document doesn't exist
# or
store.upsert(doc)  # Insert or update
```

This mirrors the R ragnar approach which has separate `ragnar_store_insert_v2()` and `ragnar_store_update_v2()` functions.

## References

- R ragnar implementation: https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar/blob/main/R/store-v2.R

description:

title: Python 3.14 support?
description:
While working on packaging for `commons`, I noticed raghilda only declares support up to 3.14. Some research on this revealed the following (only tested on my Mac).

## Summary

`requires-python` is `>=3.11, <3.14`, so raghilda does not install on Python 3.14. I tested the package on CPython 3.14.7 (macOS arm64) at `ec2edb9`. The full `task check` gate passes with no change to the source code.

## Test results on 3.14

```
pytest tests src:      362 passed, 74 skipped in 52.66s
ruff format --check:   47 files already formatted
ruff check:            All checks passed!
pyright:               0 errors, 0 warnings
```

All 74 skips are gated on credentials or on a service, and the same tests skip on 3.13: postgres (27), `OPENAI_API_KEY` (20), `NVIDIA_API_KEY` (12), Cohere (10), and one Windows-only file URI test. No test skips because of the Python version.

The one 3.14 warning comes from chromadb, not from raghilda: `DeprecationWarning: 'asyncio.iscoroutinefunction' is deprecated and slated for removal in Python 3.16` (not critical).

## A version bump won't fix it alone

`uv sync --all-extras -p 3.14` stops with this error:

```
error: Distribution `onnxruntime==1.20.1 @ registry+https://pypi.org/simple` can't be installed because it doesn't have a source distribution or wheel for the current platform

hint: You're using CPython 3.14 (`cp314`), but `onnxruntime` (v1.20.1) only has wheels with the following Python ABI tags: `cp311`, `cp312`, `cp313`, `cp313t`
```

The chain is `markitdown` -> `magika` -> `onnxruntime`. markitdown pins `magika~=0.6.1`, and magika 0.6.3 declares `onnxruntime<=1.20.1; sys_platform == "win32"`. Because uv resolves one version set for every platform, that Windows cap holds onnxruntime at 1.20.1 on all platforms. `onnxruntime` has cp314 wheels from 1.24.1 forward (1.29.0 is current).

magika 0.6.2 (the previous version) has no such cap, so one constraint clears the resolution for every platform, Windows included:

```toml
requires-python = ">=3.11, <3.15"

[tool.uv]
constraint-dependencies = ["magika!=0.6.3"]
```

This resolves to magika 0.6.2 and onnxruntime 1.29.0. The results above come from that configuration.

`uv.lock` needs a full re-lock, not an upgrade. `uv sync --upgrade-package onnxruntime` would return 1.20.1 again, because the cap and not the lockfile is what pins the version.

The constraint can go away if markitdown loosens its magika pin. magika 1.0.3 declares `onnxruntime>=1.24.1` for Python 3.14 and needs no workaround.

## What I didn't test

- Linux and Windows. Resolution succeeds for both, but I ran the test suite only on macOS arm64.
- The pgvector store tests and the live API tests. I had no docker and no API keys. CI covers both, so a CI run is worth doing before you commit to a support claim.

title: MarkdownChunker raises IndexError when CommonMark source positions include bare carriage returns
description:
MarkdownChunker can raise IndexError when the input contains bare carriage returns (\r). CommonMark treats these as line endings, but raghilda calculates source offsets by searching only for newline characters (\n).

## Environment:

- Python 3.12.5
- raghilda 0.2.0
- commonmark 0.9.2

## Failure involving the paragraph start position

```
from commonmark import Parser
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

text = "# Heading\r\n\rParagraph extracted from PDF."

ast = Parser(options={"sourcepos": True}).parse(text)
paragraph = ast.first_child.nxt
print(paragraph.sourcepos)
# [[3, 1], [3, 29]]

MarkdownChunker._paragraph_starts(text)
```

CommonMark reports the paragraph as starting on line 3:

```
paragraph [[3, 1], [3, 29]]
```

However, raghilda builds line_starts using only \n, so it has no entry for line 3. The failure occurs while calculating the start offset:

```
start = line_starts[sl - 1] + sc - 1
```

Result:

```
IndexError: list index out of range
```

## Independent failure involving the paragraph end position

```
from commonmark import Parser
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

text = "# heading\n\nparagraph\rmore"

ast = Parser(options={"sourcepos": True}).parse(text)
paragraph = ast.first_child.nxt

print(paragraph.sourcepos)
# [[3, 1], [4, 4]]

MarkdownChunker._paragraph_starts(text)
```

In this case, the paragraph start position is valid: it begins on line 3, which is present in raghilda’s line_starts list. However, CommonMark reports the paragraph ending on line 4 because it recognizes the bare \r as a line ending.

raghilda still only counts \n, so the failure occurs while calculating the end offset:

```
end = line_starts[el - 1] + ec
```

Result:

```
IndexError: list index out of range
```

## Expected behavior

The markdown source positions should be converted to character offsets without raising IndexError. Bare carriage returns should either be handled consistently with CommonMark or rejected with a controlled error.

## Actual behavior

_markdown_node_positions() assumes that every CommonMark source-position line has a corresponding entry in a line-start table constructed from \n characters only. When CommonMark recognizes bare \r characters as line endings, either the reported start or end line can exceed the available entries.

The relevant implementation is:

https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/409ee7f3d41535b5bb7469f2ddf95841c2f2fbd0/src/raghilda/_chunker.py#L217

followed by:

https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/409ee7f3d41535b5bb7469f2ddf95841c2f2fbd0/src/raghilda/_chunker.py#L223-L224

This was encountered while chunking markdown extracted from a PDF, but the issue is reproducible independently using the minimal examples above.
